business_problem: monday.com needed a reliable way to validate autonomous service agents before release because small prompt or tool-call changes could cascade into incorrect outcomes across IT, HR, and legal workflows.
solution_summary: monday.com embedded evaluation into monday Service from the start instead of treating it as a final QA step. Its AI service workforce runs as a customizable LangGraph-based ReAct agent that uses company knowledge-base articles and tools to resolve service requests. For offline testing, the team built datasets of sanitized IT tickets and ran deterministic runtime, schema, persistence, and tool-sanity checks alongside OpenEvals, AgentEvals, and LangSmith quality evaluators through the LangSmith Vitest integration, which logs every CI run as an experiment. In production, LangSmith Multi-Turn Evaluator scores complete conversation threads after custom inactivity windows, while TypeScript-based judges are deployed through a GitOps-style CLI that syncs prompts, reconciles rules, and prunes stale evaluations from the platform.

solution_components.name: LangSmith

solution_components.name: LangSmith Vitest integration

solution_components.name: Multi-Turn Evaluator

data_flow: Sanitized ticket examples and production conversations flow through the LangGraph-based service agent, offline suites run in Vitest and log traces to LangSmith, and online threads are later scored by Multi-Turn Evaluator before prompts and rules are redeployed from TypeScript definitions through CI/CD.
business_outcome: monday.com shortened the evaluation loop for customer-facing agents, increased test coverage to hundreds of examples in minutes, and added real-time production observability so AI quality regressions are caught before users see them.
